doc.title: Hubert Laws — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: The Met orchestra and joining CTI
title: Bernard Purdie and his Hitmaker placards
summary: Brown and Laws discuss whether Bernard Purdie played on the session and Laws recalls Purdie's habit of posting Hitmaker signs in studios.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Okay, but I think he might have been on Walking in Space. That’s my recollection, but I was young then. I know he’s on Oh Happy Day, because I can remember all the transitions. It goes from swing . . .
I can talk to him, because I got his number.

Last time I saw Purdie, it was in Detroit. We were doing the jazz festival in Detroit. He was with his little niece or somebody, some girl with him. That was the last time I saw him. Every time you got to a session with Bernard Purdie, he goes to set up his little placards in the window, talking about “Hitmaker.” Did you know that?
You corroborate all this. That’s legendary. Well, he’s right. All the stuff he did with Aretha. Ooo.
Yeah, he’s quite a character. Nice guy.
